name: Sanctum Aria
era_span: The Withering Era, with no year. Serenyra's and Rik'Lye's cards say Withering Era and Kaelric's "Late Withering Era"; Ameiya's states none, and the Labyrinth of Ma places them in it. The Labyrinth falls before the Sanctum Aria Concord collapsed and is unordered against Kaelric's life. Kaelric's card dates the Hall earlier than Rik'Lye's card dates the waking, so the bout in the training sanctum and the waking beneath the Citadel both follow the Hall and are unordered against each other. The cards' VE dates are not carried into the history (section 7).

members.line: High Elf of Eresse, "bloodline attenuated to the Elder Florwyn stock", Princess of Eresse and "Eresse's False Princess"; of Sanctum Aria ("neutral, Accord-aligned"), seated on the Council of Bloom and "Active in the Astral Seminary of Sanctum Aria". She declined the Grove-Spired throne for the equation, and by Isaac's ruling (2026-09-13) "the refusal was a handover, and the Venrik line holds with her assent". Her lattices, the Lunarch Crown and Crystalline Recall read and bend Aether; at the Labyrinth of Ma she saved the capital at the price of "widespread temporary collective memory loss", and her workings are paid in memories "that do not come back".

Human swordsman of the Guild Accord, the Silver Veil and Glassblade Prodigy, "Forged too quickly by the Accord's academies" and awaiting disciplinary hearings. In resonance sparring his Domain "manifested twenty-six constructs at once; the Hall collapsed inward and three cadets were lost", and "The Guild suppressed the records." His Crystal is cracked into partial selves, any surface he strikes mirrors its state, one Echoform (Kaelric-3) "is gaining autonomy", and his card names Serenyra Vale his "Rival turned confidante".

"Alchemical construct: an Aether-reactive homunculus made to recreate a soul from fractured Essence", made beneath Niran's Sanctum by "Niran, the Alchemer", whom he calls the False Mother, and "Contained by Guild Accord mandate under the Crimson-Seal Order". On his waking "his chamber liquefied into living mercury; five researchers were transmuted; Niran disappeared shortly after", and Kaelric "briefly observed" it. He mirrors others' feeling and makes none, his chains hold his memories link by link, and he wanders the lower Wellspring ruins after the Alchemer's final theorem.

Fae-touched human, the White Herald of Duskfeather, written as they: "Emissary between mortals and spirits" and a judge who must hear the guilty's grief. Raised in Velthaeir's silent cloisters and trained by Eresse's Dreamkeepers; "Independent since the collapse of the Sanctum Aria Concord", when "They stood alone against the Reflective Blight". They paid their emotional voice to seal Nihiloth, Dissolution and Vantabriel, and still see in dreams those they "mirrored" too harshly; they speak through resonance or written glyphs.

events.name: The Labyrinth of Ma
events.when: The Withering Era. While Ameiya still served as the Dreamkeepers' emissary, before the Sanctum Aria Concord collapsed. Unordered against the False Succession and against the three seals.
events.where: The capital Serenyra's card names, read here as Vaelmarr, the seat of the Grand Principality of Eresse, where the Sunroot Court sits (WORLD §3; the Elven Peoples page).
events.what: An Oneirion manifestation broke loose in the capital. Dreams stood up in its streets, solid to the hand. The Dreamkeepers sent in the emissary they had trained to stand between mortals and spirits. Ameiya went down into the streets where people were caught. They folded the lamplight into layered shields and held them over the doorways. The shields hummed with the fear of the people behind them, and the motes about the herald took its colour. Serenyra came to the edge of the manifestation with the Aether Chord Staff. She wrote a lattice around the whole of it and drew each loose thread into the geometry, from the edge inward. When every thread was in, the manifestation held one shape and stood still. The streets emptied of what had been dreamed. Then the capital forgot. The forgetting was wide, and in time it passed. Ameiya's shields were still up over the doorways when the lattice closed, and Serenyra found the herald there when it was done. Their eyes were still turning through the colours of the crowd. She watched them until the colours slowed. Took: Serenyra, the capital saved, and the city's forgetting laid at her working; her card keeps both. A herald who held the streets while she closed the lattice; Ameiya, a street held under folded light until another hand's lattice closed over the whole of it; the crowd's fear in their motes; an archmagus who came afterward to watch their eyes.

events.name: The bout in the training sanctum
events.when: The Withering Era. After the Hall collapsed on the three cadets and the Guild suppressed its record, while Kaelric stood under Guild observation for his surges. Unordered against the waking beneath the Citadel.
events.where: The Concord Citadel (WORLD §4), in one of the training sanctums of the City Below (The Concord Citadel page).
events.what: Lurein Velos had counselled patience and been set aside. After the Hall he asked for a reading of his student from outside the Guild's own halls. Sanctum Aria keeps with the Accord and holds itself neutral. It sent Serenyra. She stood at the centre of the sanctum with the Lunarch Crown on her brow. Kaelric was told to strike until she had seen enough. He drew Mirrhalion. Every blow he put into the field around her went out of it as light. Each surface he strikes mirrors his Crystal for an instant. Her field was the surface he struck, and at each blow it showed her the crack through the prism core. Lurein called the bout. Kaelric kept on. He struck faster, and the delayed selves he leaves behind him came in on the field one after another. Each of them showed her the same crack. Serenyra lowered the staff. The bout was over. She gave Lurein her reading, and it agreed with his counsel; the Guild filed it beside its own and kept Kaelric in the field. The next time she came to the Citadel he asked for the bout again. She gave it to him. He asked again after that. In time he stopped striking and asked her what the field had shown. She told him. Took: Kaelric, a bout he could not win, fought on after his instructor called it; the one surface that showed him his own Crystal, and the one reader who would tell him what it showed; Serenyra, the Accord's prodigy read at every blow; a reading the Accord filed and did not follow; a rival who kept coming back for the bout.

events.name: The waking beneath the Citadel
events.when: The Withering Era. After the Hall. Unordered against the bout.
events.where: Beneath the Concord Citadel (WORLD §4), in the laboratories beneath Niran's Sanctum. Rik'Lye's card puts the laboratories beneath the Sanctum and the five pillars beneath the Citadel; this record sets the chamber where the pillars stand. No page places Niran's Sanctum.
events.what: The Alchemer opened the vessel. The Guild had set blades of Kaelric's Division at the chamber door for the opening, and he was one of them. The glyphs on the vessel's skin began to pulse. Then the chamber liquefied. Floor, walls and benches ran together into living mercury, and every surface in the room became a moving mirror. Kaelric's reflections were in all of it. Every one of them reacted violently to the thing that had woken. He was pulled back from the door, and the door was shut. Five researchers had been inside. When the mercury stilled they were crystal pillars, and they hum there still. The Alchemer was gone shortly after. The Alchemer's own entry named the vessel an experimental containment success. The Guild would not write that down openly, and it wrote nothing honest in its place. Took: Kaelric, a brief sight of the vessel waking, cut off at the door; his reflections turned violent in a room made of mirrors; a second record the Guild would not keep straight, after his Hall; Rik'Lye, a waking into a chamber gone to mercury, with a blade at the door whose reflections reacted violently to his presence; five pillars where the researchers had stood; the Alchemer gone shortly after.

ties.summary: His card names her so; in the training sanctum her field showed his crack at every blow, he kept coming back for the bout, and in time she told him what it showed.
He stood at the chamber door when the vessel woke, and his reflections reacted violently to the presence; each card names the other.
Both cards carry Sanctum Aria and Eresse; at the Labyrinth of Ma the herald held the streets under folded light while the archmagus closed the lattice.

outward.wants: The crown that holds the Grove-Spired throne by her assent. Isaac's ruling of 2026-09-13 puts the Venrik line there, and c10 holds Karo and Asta Venrik; its outward line for Asta names Serenyra. Maeron Iskare (c30) is the other card that names her, with "Mutual respect".
The Accord officer who will sit his disciplinary hearing. The Guild Accord page gives Arbitration "adjudication of Trials of Resonance". No card holds Lurein Velos or Kaelric-3.

The Accord office that keeps his containment under the Crimson-Seal mandate. The Guild Accord page gives Research and Archives "artifact containment". Kaelzar's card (c16) names "Niran · Former overseer of Echo Containment"; whether that Niran is his False Mother no card says.
One of the people they "mirrored" too harshly, someone Echo-Judgment weighed wrong after the voice was paid and who still carries the verdict. The card names none.

card_contradictions: Serenyra's surname. Kaelric's card: "Serenyra Vale · Rival turned confidante; often the only one who sees his fractures." (IX). Maeron's card: "Serenyra Vale · Mutual respect." (`Maeron Iskare · The Silent Oracle.md`, IX). Her own card: "Name · Serenyra Vaelith." (I).

Two bearers of the Silver Veil. Kaelric's card: "Kaelric Varnier · The Silver Veil" and "Called · The Silver Veil. The Glassblade Prodigy." (I). Serenyra's card: "Also known as · The Silver Veil · High Archivist of Resonance · The Princess of Eresse." (I), and under Aurevane, "The Silver Veil, the Refraction Field, the Lunarch Crown" (III).

Sanctum Aria, standing and collapsed. Serenyra's card, in the present tense: "Active in the Astral Seminary of Sanctum Aria." (I). Ameiya's card: "Independent since the collapse of the Sanctum Aria Concord." (I) and "The Sanctum Aria Concord · Collapsed." (IX). Whether the Concord is the order, a compact of it or a body beside it, neither card says, and no page defines any of them.

Niran. Rik'Lye's card: "Niran, the Alchemer · Creator and mother-figure. He calls her the False Mother. Missing since the Abython breach." with its own note, "canon's Niran is Niran Yukari, a man; the card's is a woman" (IX). Kaelzar's card: "Niran · Former overseer of Echo Containment", with the note that canon's Niran Yukari is a living practitioner of the Yukari Enclave "with no containment role" (`Kaelzar · The Forge That Roars.md`, IX).

The card dates. Kaelric's card: "Era: Late Withering Era, card date VE 927" and "During resonance sparring at card date VE 925" (I). Rik'Lye's card: "Era: Withering Era, card date after VE 920" (I) and "Containment Breach, Abython Reaction, card date VE 926" (X). The two cards agree with each other. The Concordance of Ages sets the Voyager Era at 000 to 070 IC and the Withering Era from 645 IC, and WORLD §1 lists "VE 927" among the terms that fit no era.

A Division the Accord lacks. Kaelric's card: "Guild Accord, Division of Resonant Arms *(unattested)*" (I). The Guild Accord page gives five Divisions, Strategic, Enforcement, Arbitration, Research and Archives, Logistics and Supply, and "The sixth and unspoken Division", the Black Concord.

The Hall and the hearing. Kaelric's card: "The Guild suppressed the records." of the Hall (I, Catalyst Event), and disciplinary hearings "for reckless Domain manifestation during a training exercise" (I, Affiliation). Whether the hearing concerns the Hall, or a later exercise, the card does not say.
Ameiya's speech. "They rarely speak, and never about their own work" (I, Gloss rights). "They speak only through resonance or written glyphs." (VI, The Silenced Voice).
The Grove-Spired throne. Serenyra's refusal and Karo Venrik's surrendered succession stand on two cards; c10, section 7, item 3, quotes both beside Asta's crown and Isaac's ruling. Not repeated here.
